At last night's Emmy Awards ceremony, Apple TV defeated rivals including HBO to become the most awarded platform. Below is how HBO's helmsman Casey Bloys responded to Apple's victory.

HBO's CEO highly praised Apple TV's outstanding performance, but also acknowledged that competing with a company worth a trillion dollars is 'somewhat daunting'

Apple TV has long been compared to HBO, with both prioritising quality over quantity. Apple has even sometimes been called the 'new HBO'.

Last night's Emmys further confirmed this notion, as Apple TV outpaced HBO, Netflix, and other platforms to become the most awarded platform of the night.

Apple TV took home a total of 29 awards, becoming 'the most awarded network of the year', with shows like 'Widow's Bay' standing out particularly. HBO came in second with 21 awards.

After the Emmy Awards ceremony, HBO executive Casey Bloys was interviewed by Deadline and asked about his thoughts on Apple's performance. His response was as follows:

DEADLINE: What are your thoughts on Apple TV's performance this time? They became the most awarded platform at the Emmys for the first time. What's your view? BLOYS: Well, I'm actually quite pleased, because I think they're very formidable competitors, Zack and Jamie. We've always had strong rivals — Showtime, FX, AMC, Netflix, Amazon — so with Apple, everyone keeps us on our toes, and that's when I do my best work. They're a company worth a trillion dollars, and that is indeed somewhat daunting, but we'll keep doing what we've always done, which is making the best programmes.

Bloys joined HBO in 2004 and has served as Head of Programming since 2016. His track record speaks for itself, and his response to Apple's victory was largely gracious and sincerely congratulatory.

However, the most interesting part of his response was this line: 'They're a company worth a trillion dollars, and that is indeed somewhat daunting.'

We're not sure about Apple TV's internal budget, but there's no doubt that Apple as a whole far exceeds the financial resources of most competitors, including HBO.

Coincidentally, Paramount is currently actively pursuing the acquisition of HBO (along with the rest of Warner Bros. Discovery's assets), hoping to compete more effectively with tech giants like Apple and Amazon.

Does size automatically confer an advantage? Perhaps. But many networks have proven that in producing content audiences love, funding is only a small part of the equation.

Apple TV costs US$14.99 per month, and is also available through the Apple One bundle subscription.
